claim.purpose: Execute #5662 as the bounded WP-15 visual and runtime presentation polish lane for the flagship Unity Observatory

initial.title: [v0.91.8][WP-15][unity][demo] Polish flagship Polis Observatory visual and runtime presentation
initial.goal: Turn the functional Observatory stage into a beautiful, coherent, truthful Unity control environment that demonstrates the living Polis to investors and inhabitants.
initial.required_outcome: The intended FastWork Unity project opens and plays one polished Observatory scene whose camera, environment, lighting, fixed operator shell, runtime state, and bounded interactions work together, with direct proof at 1920x1080 and 2560x1440.
declared_scope: Flagship Observatory scene composition and hero camera
Terrain, platform, ramp, and architectural continuity
Lighting, emission, environment, and material readability
Fixed screen-space operator dashboard and clear iconography
Truthful CSM and Polis runtime presentation states
Agent inspection, event observation, governance and evidence visibility, and bounded communication
Direct Unity-MCP, Play Mode, and visual proof
authority_boundary: #5662 owns final visual and runtime presentation polish for the flagship Unity Observatory
#5354 owns WP-15 convergence and consumes this issue's proof
#4739, #4741, and #5332 remain the closed tooling and compatibility prerequisites
Licensed asset packs remain external to Git and are not republished
No player binaries, replacement owner binaries, WP-14A acceptance, or unsupported production-cloud claims
initial.task_boundary: Polish and prove only the repository-owned Observatory scene, controller, UI, contract, and proof surfaces while authoring against the operator-provisioned FastWork Unity project.
deliverables: Composed flagship Observatory environment and stable hero camera
Fixed readable operator shell with clear icons and internal scrolling
Truthful live, degraded, disconnected, and demo runtime states
Supported agent, event, governance, evidence, and communication interactions
Retained intended-project Play Mode proof at both target resolutions
Durable routing for every tooling anomaly encountered
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: the hero view has a clear focal Observatory structure, grounded foreground, readable middle ground and background, and a deliberate route into the environment
AC-2: the camera does not clip major architecture or reveal accidental voids, floating terrain edges, disconnected ramps, or unfinished staging geometry
AC-3: lighting preserves material detail and depth, uses cyan as a controlled accent, and keeps dark regions intentionally readable
AC-4: UI text and icons are crisp, aligned, non-overlapping, and legible at 1920x1080 and 2560x1440 with a fixed dashboard and only internal scrolling
AC-5: the shell explicitly identifies live, degraded, disconnected, and demo states and never presents fixture data as live Polis truth
AC-6: live mode consumes repository-owned runtime contracts for supported agent, event, health, governance, evidence, and communication fields while unsupported fields remain explicit non-claims
AC-7: an operator can select an agent or subsystem, inspect current state, observe event flow, and send a bounded communication through the supported contract or receive an exact fail-closed reason
AC-8: direct Unity proof identifies the intended FastWork project, loaded FlagshipObservatoryStage, clean Play Mode result, and retained 1920x1080 and 2560x1440 captures
AC-9: focused validation passes without building a player binary or replacement owner binary and without copying licensed payloads into Git
AC-10: every encountered Unity-MCP, editor, runtime, asset, or proof-tool anomaly is retained in #5662 or routed to a named follow-up
dependencies: Operator-provisioned FastWork Unity project and licensed local asset packs
Repository-installed Unity-MCP CLI and #4739 alignment probe
repo_inputs: operator-provided current-stage screenshot and Observatory dashboard visual direction
non_goals: Do not build standalone player binaries
Do not build replacement ADL, C-SDLC, Unity-MCP, or other owner binaries
Do not republish licensed asset packs or add multi-gigabyte asset payloads to Git
Do not absorb WP-14A platform acceptance or unrelated release-tail work
Do not claim production cloud integration, complete investor readiness, or unsupported runtime semantics
Do not treat static source checks as Unity visual or runtime proof
initial.plan_summary: Align the intended live project, establish a visual baseline, polish spatial composition and lighting, refine the fixed runtime shell, exercise supported interactions, then retain direct dual-resolution Play Mode proof and synchronize only repository-owned source.

steps.action: Re-prove intended project, active MCP endpoint, loaded flagship scene, and clean editor state; capture the current baseline
Correct hero camera, terrain and platform continuity, spatial hierarchy, and exposed staging defects through Unity-MCP or editor tooling
Tune lighting, emission, environment, and material readability for a controlled cinematic presentation
Refine the fixed operator shell, icons, truth modes, and supported runtime interactions
Capture direct 1920x1080 and 2560x1440 Play Mode proof, synchronize only repository-owned source, and run focused validation
Run bounded pre-publication review, resolve findings, and retain truthful WP-15 handoff evidence

risks: Licensed prefab and material dependencies may not serialize portably into the tracked scene
Live editor and MCP endpoint may drift between project instances
The current camera and platform arrangement can expose large voids at wide aspect ratios
Runtime contracts may not yet expose every desired governance, evidence, or communication field
UI Toolkit scaling can become illegible or overlapping across target resolutions
Visual tuning can mask runtime truth unless state labeling remains fail closed
invariants: The intended project and loaded scene are proven before mutation or claims
Licensed assets remain external and untracked
Runtime truth is explicit and fixture data is never labeled live
The first Play Mode frame reads as the Observatory
The dashboard is fixed and only bounded internal windows scroll
No player or replacement owner binary is built
Tooling anomalies become durable issue evidence
stop_conditions: The live Unity editor is attached to a different project than the intended FastWork Observatory
MCP project identity cannot be proven or mutations target an ambiguous endpoint
Unity reports compile errors that prevent safe scene mutation
A required change would copy or publish licensed asset payloads
Runtime communication requires an unsupported or secret-bearing direct AWS operation
The work would need to absorb WP-14A or unrelated release-tail scope
review_prompts: Does the first Play Mode frame read as one deliberate Observatory rather than a staging pile?
Are camera, terrain, ramps, lighting, materials, UI, and runtime state coherent at both target resolutions?
Can every live, degraded, disconnected, demo, governance, evidence, and communication claim be traced to direct supported proof?
Does the diff contain only repository-owned publishable source and exclude licensed payloads and binary output?
Were all tooling anomalies retained or routed with current reproduction evidence?
operator_constraints: Work only in the bound #5662 FastWork worktree and intended Unity project
Create the issue-bound goal before implementation
Use Unity-MCP or editor tools for scene mutation and direct proof
Use repository-installed binaries and permission-safe process checks
No raw gh, broad process scans, cloud fallback, secret exposure, player builds, or replacement binaries

validation_lanes.proof_role: Prove repository-owned Unity project structure, runtime contract, and guarded asset publication boundary
Prove bounded source hygiene and absence of whitespace or patch corruption
Prove intended project identity, loaded flagship scene, Play Mode behavior, and dual-resolution visual presentation
validation_lanes.defer_reason: The alignment probe establishes the prerequisite identity; direct Unity-MCP Play Mode and screenshot operations complete the visual proof during execution.

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on project ambiguity, compile errors, cloud fallback, unlabelled fixture data, unsupported runtime claims, licensed payload publication, player or replacement binary builds, missing dual-resolution proof, or unrecorded tooling anomalies.
